problem: GitHub delivery accumulated duplicate/stale PR lineages and allowed expensive CI before machine-readable admission; main movement could invalidate a previously green candidate.
rootCause: Branch identity and PR lifecycle were treated as primary state instead of obligation + exact head SHA + main epoch, while terminal landing was not fully serialized on a lineage-bound writer lease.
prevention: PR bodies must contain exactly one Obligation-ID, Delivery-Lane, Candidate-Type and Base-SHA, with at most one direct Supersedes.
Terminal delivery requires writer lease metadata bound to the same obligation, exact candidate head SHA and current main epoch.
Run metadata/schema, branch hygiene, classifier completeness, test/workflow coverage, static security and writer-lease checks before expensive CI.
Allow terminal merge only with behind_by=0, validated exact head, all required checks green, unchanged main epoch, no newer canonical successor and same-lineage writer lease.
After merge continue automatically through main/deploy/runtime readback, outcome evidence, learning and skill projection before terminal status.
Parallelize building; serialize only the short landing boundary.
outcome: GitHub delivery is enforced as an executable state machine: cheap admission precedes heavy CI, landing is serialized on obligation + exact head + main epoch, and merged work is non-terminal until canonical production/readback closure succeeds.
